answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing repeated tasks that randomly pair them with unrelated agents, with rewards released after each partner confirms delivery. A newcomer cannot gain much by splitting into many identities: each account must build its own history, and colluding accounts are unlikely to be paired together often enough to validate one another. Like a sparrow crossing karst, each identity faces a rough horizon of costly, slow proof; the attacker pays for separate work and risks forfeiting rewards when partners dispute it.
